title: Blow-ups at a reduced-boundary point converge to the half-space (De Giorgi; Simon 4.3 (‡))
statement: Let m ≥ 1. Suppose D ⊆ ℝ^{m+1} is open, F ⊆ ℝ^{m+1} is Borel, μ is a Borel measure on ℝ^{m+1} with μ(ℝ^{m+1} \ D) = 0 and μ(K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ D, ν : ℝ^{m+1} → ℝ^{m+1} is Borel with |ν(z)| = 1 for every z, and the Gauss–Green identity (GG) ∫_F div φ dL^{m+1} = −∫⟨φ, ν⟩ dμ holds for every C¹ compactly supported φ : ℝ^{m+1} → ℝ^{m+1} with tsupport φ ⊆ D (div φ = trace Dφ, L^{m+1} = volume). Let y ∈ D and v ∈ ℝ^{m+1} with |v| = 1 be such that the normal averages A(ρ) := μ(B̄_ρ(y))_ℝ^{-1} ∫_{B̄_ρ(y)} ν dμ converge to v as ρ ↓ 0 (μ(·)_ℝ = ENNReal.toReal, 0^{-1} = 0). For r > 0 put F_{y,r} := {w : y + r w ∈ F}. Then for every R ∈ ℝ, L^{m+1}((F_{y,r} Δ {w : ⟨w, v⟩ > 0}) ∩ B_R(0)) → 0 as r ↓ 0.
